newsitem.title: UK: Major pledges to cut UK inheritance tax.
newsitem.headline: Major pledges to cut UK inheritance tax.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Friday that the Conservative Party would abolish inheritance tax after having reduced and then scrapped capital gains tax.
"Over time our next target is to remove the burden of inheritance tax," Major said in his keynote speech to the party's annual conference in Bournemouth.
He pledged to "reduce and then abolish" capital gains tax to encourage wealth creation for the future.

Echoing Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's speech on Thursday, Major said the Conservative government's priority was to cut the basic rate of income tax to 20 pence in the pound "as we can afford it."
Major said that if his Conservative Party wins the next election, due to be held by May 1997, it will raise spending on the National Health Service by more than the rate of inflation year after year.
In what was billed as a key pledge, Major said in a speech prepared for delivery to the conference: "Today, I give you a health service guarantee."
"Our manifesto will pledge that the NHS will get more, over and above inflation, year on year on year on year on year through the next Conservative government."
